content:
Sounds like the program is freezing. Sometimes you may get a 'not responding' notice at the top ?

It's possible another program is intervening and locking out Thunderbird. The most likely culprit and place to start is the Firewall and the Anti-Virus.

1. Firewall This may the default supplied with OS or it may be controlled by an Anti-Virus product you installed. To ensure your Firewall is not blocking any access, it is important to access Firewall and set up the Thunderbird program as allowed. It's no use simply turning off Firewall, because A) you cannot operate that way, it's not safe. B) if it's controlled by an Anti-Virus you installed then the default will take over, so it's still operating. Confirm the Firewall as Thunderbird program as allowed.

2. Anti-Virus Q: What anti-virus are you using ? If Avast or AVG then disable the 'mail shield' to see if it improves the situation. That email shield is notorious for causing problems.

Whatever, Anti-Virus you are using , please make sure it's not allowed to scan your Thunderbird folder which contains Profiles. Set up an exclusion to not scan that Thunderbird folder, so it does not scan any contents. eg: C:Users/username/Appdata/Roaming/Thunderbird

Otherwise, every file that gets opened will get scanned meaning it blocks Thunderbird from using it's own profile files. Anything you download, move etc, that involves opening files. If you use Imap account then there's much jibber jabber with the server and various files get opened.

Completely shutting down computer is a bit drastic. Are you saying if you right click on Task Bar' and select open Task Manager to see all running programs, when you select Thunderbird and click on 'End Task' - it does not work ?

content:
As Toad-Hall mentions, the clickable links thing is a Windows issue, not Thunderbird's. Thunderbird relies on Windows to tell it what to do when it encounters a web link. It is unrelated to your Yahoo issue, which I understand is now working correctly.

If Windows 7 doesn't let you change the defaults for Firefox, it's because it already is the default. However, Windows can get confused, especially earlier version like Windows 7, which is why it can help to "tickle" it by changing the setting to something else, then back to the original. If you don't have a second web browser installed, Internet Explorer is still available. It's useless as a web browser, but for this purpose it will do. If it's not currently installed, got to Windows' <Control Panel | Programs and Features | Turn Windows Features Off or On> and turn on Internet Explorer 11. Now you can go back to <Control Panel | Default Programs> and change the default web browser to IE, then back to Firefox. This might help - I can't guarantee it.

Another possible factor is that some emails that are in HTML format are incorrectly coded so that web links are not clickable. This is the fault of the sender, not of Thunderbird or Windows. If you find that SOME emails have clickable links, but others from different senders DO have clickable links, this is probably the case. A workaround is to display the message in Plain Text format - Thunderbird will usually recognize the link on its own and make it clickable for you. To change the viewing format, in Thunderbird go to menu item <View | Message Body As...> and choose Plain Text. You may find that the links are now clickable.
